# Cases and categories

The case registry IS the validation design (ADR-0069 clause 4), not a set of examples. Every case
carries a category, a scientific reason for inclusion, fixed seeds, an expected behaviour, a kill
criterion, and a split assignment.

## The five axes, and why each is separate

* **Stacking geometry** is the primary axis: the build method decides how many layers a cut crosses,
  and that is the dominant term in everything downstream.
* **Reclaim method** is independent of the build. It is held at chevron so the comparison is clean,
  and `G01_chevron` serves as the full-face reference rather than being duplicated as an `R01`.
* **Input variability** is the autocorrelation of the incoming stream, which decides whether the
  layers a cut crosses are independent enough for the bed to help at all.
* **Segregation regime** covers whether kinetic sieving biases the cut, and whether the two species
  have different enough repose angles to stratify.
* **Controls** are three, each with a numerical kill criterion. Without them a plausible wrong answer
  is indistinguishable from a right one.

## Splits

By seed AND input structure. Splitting by seed alone would leak the SHAPE of the stream, so a model
trained on every structure and tested on the same structures learns the four shapes rather than the
physics. All cases below are held out of surrogate training entirely.

## By category

### stacking-geometry

How the pile was built.

- [`G01_chevron`](G01_chevron.md) - VRR clearly below cone shell and above chevcon; layers crossed per cut close to the pass count
- [`G02_windrow`](G02_windrow.md) - VRR near chevron; a smaller toe-minus-apex coarse delta than chevron at the same Sr
- [`G03_coneshell`](G03_coneshell.md) - VRR in the 0.2 to 0.35 band, consistent with the published cone shell floor
- [`G04_strata`](G04_strata.md) - VRR between chevron and cone shell
- [`G05_chevcon`](G05_chevcon.md) - The lowest VRR of the five, at or below about 0.15

### reclaim-method

How the pile was taken back.

- [`R02_bucketwheel`](R02_bucketwheel.md) - VRR above full-face and below end reclaim
- [`R03_end`](R03_end.md) - VRR well above full-face; the reclaimed stream visibly lags the input rather than averaging it
- [`R04_loader`](R04_loader.md) - The worst VRR of the reclaim axis, plausibly close to 1 (little or no blending)

### input-variability

What the incoming stream looked like.

- [`V01_short_range`](V01_short_range.md) - Blending efficiency against the 1/N bound the highest of the four V cases
- [`V02_long_range`](V02_long_range.md) - VRR close to 1 and efficiency far below V01; the bed barely helps
- [`V03_trending`](V03_trending.md) - VRR may look acceptable while the reclaimed mean drifts; the drift must be visible on the stream plot
- [`V04_bimodal`](V04_bimodal.md) - Reclaimed grade histogram visibly bimodal despite a VRR below 0.4

### segregation-regime

How strongly the material sorted itself.

- [`S01_strong_sieving`](S01_strong_sieving.md) - A large positive toe-minus-apex coarse-fraction delta; cut composition varying with the reclaim front position
- [`S02_stratifying`](S02_stratifying.md) - Alternating coarse and fine bands visible in the cutaway; a larger segregation index than S01 at the same Sr is not expected, the signature is the layering, not the magnitude

### control

Controls with numerical kill criteria.

- [`C01_perfect_mixer`](C01_perfect_mixer.md) - Achieved VRR equal to 1/N within the multi-seed band
- [`C02_no_segregation`](C02_no_segregation.md) - Every lot in the pile still carries exactly the coarse fraction of the truck it came from. The aggregate toe-minus-apex delta is not expected to be zero: different dumps carry different size distributions and land in different places, so the geometry alone produces a small spatial pattern. Measured at Sr = 0 it is about -0.01, against about +0.44 at Sr = 1, so the solver contribution is two orders of magnitude larger than the geometric one.
- [`C03_starvation`](C03_starvation.md) - The pile empties, the run reports starvation, and no tonnage is negative or NaN
